title: Ten Ones Make a New Unit
objective: Ten individual ones can be bundled and treated as a single new unit — one ten — the conceptual heart of place value (unitizing).
studentQuestion: If I bundle these, what do I have now?
newIdea: Unitizing — a group of ten counted as one thing, not ten things.

teaching.setup: 10 loose counters, counted individually to confirm there are 10.
teaching.see: We counted 10 loose ones. What if we bundle them together?
teaching.break: Physically bundle the 10 ones into a single rod/bundle.
teaching.build: Name the bundle: this is one ten.
teaching.transform: 10 loose ones — 1 bundle of ten — same value, a new countable unit.

check.prompt: Unbundle and recount the loose ones to confirm there are still 10.

examples.second: A second group of 10 bundled the same way, compared to the first.
examples.transfer: Given 2 separate bundles of ten (already made), state the total without unbundling (20).

mastery.evidence: Correctly states a bundle of ten still represents 10 ones, and unbundles/recounts to confirm without prompting.
